items.stem: What is the purpose of HTTP?

Transfers files between a client and a server
Transfers web pages from a web server to a browser
Accesses email kept on the server so it can be synchronised across several devices

items.stem: Explain the difference between POP3 and IMAP.
items.answer: POP3 downloads emails to one device and usually deletes them from the server; IMAP keeps emails on the server and synchronises them across several devices.

items.stem: Describe the role of the transport layer when a web page is sent.
items.answer: Splits the data into segments, adds port numbers and sequence numbers; TCP checks for errors, acknowledges receipt and resends lost segments; reassembles in order at the destination.

items.stem: Omar downloads a web page. Name the application layer protocol used and describe what happens to the data at each of the four layers of the TCP/IP stack as it is sent.

items.stem: In circuit switching, what happens before data is sent?
options: Routers decide a new route for each packet
A dedicated path is set up between sender and receiver for the whole communication
The data is split into packets that take different routes
items.answer: A dedicated path is set up between sender and receiver for the whole communication
items.markingKey: Circuit switching: the route is reserved; all data follows it in order.

items.stem: Explain why packet switching makes better use of a network than circuit switching.
items.answer: Links are shared by packets from many users and are only used when data is sent; in circuit switching the reserved path is unavailable to others even when idle.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain why circuit switching may be preferred for a live video call.
items.answer: The dedicated path gives a constant bandwidth and data arrives in order with little delay or jitter.

items.stem: A packet sent from GreenLeaf Pharmacy in Manila has a TTL (hop limit) of 16; each router decrements it by 1 and discards the packet when it reaches 0. The best route passes through 8 routers. State whether the packet reaches its destination and explain why routers use a TTL.
items.answer: Yes: it arrives with TTL 8. The TTL stops packets circulating for ever in routing loops.
items.markingKey: 16 − 8 (1); conclusion (1); reason for TTL (1) [3]

items.stem: SkyLink Airways in Lisbon is choosing a network service for its video conferencing. Evaluate the use of packet switching rather than circuit switching for real-time communication such as video calls.
items.answer: Points in favour: efficient sharing of links; resilience as packets can be re-routed; cheaper; works well with buffering and QoS. Points against / limitations: variable delay (latency, jitter) and packets arriving out of order or lost can disrupt real-time audio and video; circuit switching gives a guaranteed constant connection. Conclusion: packet switching is now used for most calls because of efficiency, with protocols to reduce jitter.

[6]

items.stem: A packet leaves Kathmandu with a time-to-live (TTL) of 8. Each router decreases the TTL by 1 and discards the packet if it reaches 0. The route to the destination passes through 5 routers. What happens to the packet?
options: It is sent back to the sender with TTL 8
items.answer: It arrives with TTL 3
items.markingKey: TTL after 5 routers would be 8 − 5 = 3; it arrives.

items.answer: It arrives with TTL 2
items.markingKey: TTL after 2 routers would be 4 − 2 = 2; it arrives.

items.stem: Orbit Games Studio in Singapore is choosing a network service for its video conferencing. Discuss the use of packet switching rather than circuit switching for real-time communication such as video calls.
items.answer: Points in favour: efficient sharing of links; resilience as packets can be re-routed; cheaper; works well with buffering and QoS. Points against / limitations: variable delay (latency, jitter) and packets arriving out of order or lost can disrupt real-time audio and video; circuit switching gives a guaranteed constant connection. Conclusion: packet switching is now used for most calls because of efficiency, with protocols to reduce jitter.
